lines.li: [us] Is winter hard where you live?
[them] Winter is most of the year where I live, so we're good at it.
[us] How do you pass the long nights?
[them,their:tribal] Stories and sewing, and then more stories.
[them] Mending, quarreling and sleeping, in about equal measure.
[us] That sounds almost cozy.
[them] It is, until the woodpile runs low.
[them] Where I live, cold means a blanket at night, not this.
[us] You'll get used to it.
[them] I'd rather not have to.
[them] Summer at home is two weeks of mud and biting flies.
[us] And the rest of the year?
[them] Snow, and we like it better.
[them] At home it rains every afternoon this time of year, you could set a clock by it.
[us] Every afternoon?
[them] Every one, and the frogs sing about it all night.
[them] The woods at home will be full of birdsong by now.
[us] Do you miss it?
[them,their:tribal] I hear it in my sleep, so I am never quite away.
[them] A little, it's the best time to walk under the trees.
[them] The leaves will be turning at home, red and gold as far as you can see.
[us] It sounds beautiful.
[them] It is, for a week, and then it's raking.
[them] The grass at home will be up to a rider's knees by now.
[us] Plenty of grazing, then.
[them] Plenty, and plenty of wind to go with it.
[them] This time of year the wind across our plains could knock a cart over.
[us] Do you ever get used to it?
[them] You stop hearing it, and then one day it stops and you can't sleep.
[them] The passes at home will just be opening.
[us] Is it a hard climb?
[them] Hard enough that we only make it when we must, and we sing the whole way.
[us] For courage?
[them] For breath, if you sing you can't complain.
[them] The passes at home are usually snowed shut by now.
[us] Will you get back?
[them] The long way round, which is long indeed.
[them] The sea at home will be throwing itself at the rocks this time of year.
[us] Do the boats still go out?
[them] Only the brave and the hungry, and they're mostly the same people.
[them] At home the boats are out from dawn to dusk in summer.
[us] Do you fish yourself?
[them] Everyone does a little, it's that or go hungry.
[them] At home we sleep through the afternoons in summer, it's too hot for anything else.
[us] And work at night?
[them] Work, market, weddings, all of it, by lamplight.
[them] Your nights are softer than ours, in the desert they bite.
[us] Bite?
[them] Cold enough to stiffen the water skins by morning.
[us] What's winter like in {TOWN}?
[them,home:frozen] Long, white and quiet, the way we like it.
[them,home:hot|home:desert] Hardly a winter at all, the nights are cool and that's the end of it.
[them] Dark early, and everyone indoors telling the same old stories.
[us] The same ones every year?
[them] Every year, and we laugh in the same places.
[us] What's summer like in {TOWN}?
[them,home:desert|home:hot] Hot enough that nobody moves between noon and dusk.
[them,home:frozen] Short, and everybody tries to cram a whole year into it.
[them] Long days, short tempers, and everyone out late.
[us] That sounds about right.
[them,their:lowtech] Spring at home means mud, and lambs, and everyone in a better mood.
[them] Spring at home means mud on every boot and everyone in a better mood.
[us] Mud I can live with.
[them] So can we, for the mood.
[them] Fall at home means wood smoke in the air and apples on every table.
[us] We could use a few of those apples.
[them,role:trader] I might have a sack, for the right price.
[them] Next time, if I remember, and if I don't eat them first.
[us] What's it like, living in the marshes?
[them] Everything is wet, everything floats or sinks, and the eels are as long as my leg.
[us] I'm not sure I'd sleep.
[them] You'd sleep fine, the frogs sing you down.
[us] Is it hilly around {TOWN}?
[them] Hills and more hills, my legs were made for them.
[us] Do you miss them?
[them] Only when I've walked on flat ground for a week.
[us] What's the land like at home?
[them] Grass to the edge of the sky, and wind in it all day.
[us] No trees at all?
[them] A few, and we've named every one of them.
[them] It's gentle country around {TOWN}, not too hot and not too cold.
[us] That sounds easy.
[them] Easy to live in and hard to leave, that's the trouble with it.
[them] At home you're always walking uphill, both ways.
[us] That can't be true.
[them] Come and try it, then.
[us] Where does {TOWN} get its water?
[them,their:lowtech] Deep wells, and the keeper of each well is the most important person in town.
[them] Deep wells and good pumps, and someone who guards them with their life.
[us] I'd want that job.
[them] Nobody wants it, the whole town shouts at you when it runs low.
[us] What do your people eat, up where nothing grows?
[them,their:tribal] What we hunt, what we dry, and what we trade the furs for.
[them] What we can store, what we can trade for, and a lot of soup.
[us] A lot of soup?
[them] You'd be amazed what goes into soup when it's cold enough.
[us] Any trouble on the road?
[them,town:site] Nothing that came near us, though we gave {SITE} a wide berth.
[them] None, and I'm not complaining.
[us] Long may it last.
[us] Do the animals trouble you out on the road?
[them,winter] In winter they're all hungry, so we keep the fire high.
[them,their:tribal] We know their ways, and they know ours.
[them] Only the hungry ones, and we keep a fire going at night.
[us] Sensible.
[us] Do you pass any old ruins on the road?
[them,their:tribal] We walk around them, the old places are not for the living.
[them,their:hightech] Plenty, and anything worth taking was taken long ago.
[them] Some, and I don't stop, old places have a way of keeping people.
[us] I've heard the same.
[us] You must be our nearest neighbors, I think.
[them] Near enough to borrow salt, and far enough not to hear you argue.
[us] That's the best kind of near.
[them] Every time I make this trip, I swear it's the last.
[us] And yet here you are.
[them] Here I am, and already dreading the way back.
[them] Nobody sensible walks these roads after dark.
[us] Then don't set off too late.
[them,role:guest] I'm in no hurry, your beds are better than the road's.
[them] I won't, I value my neck.
[us] Your boots have seen some miles.
[them] More than I have, they've been mended twice.
[us] And you?
[them] I've been mended more than twice.
[us] How do you find your way out there?
[them] The stones point, the rivers remember, and the stars never lie.
[us] And when it's cloudy?
[them] Then you ask the nearest old woman.
[us] How do you find your way all that distance?
[them] Maps, mostly, and they're wrong about half the time.
[us] And the other half?
[them] The other half they're wrong in ways I've learned to expect.
[them] My pack animals are tired, and so am I.
[us] Rest a while, then.
[them] A while is all I've got.
[us] Do you like traveling in company?
[them,trait:Abrasive] I like it better when the company keeps quiet.
[them,trait:Kind] Always, a road is shorter with someone to talk to.
[them] Most of the time, until someone starts to sing.
[us] I'll keep my singing to myself, then.
[them] Is this rain going to stop, do you think?
[us] It always does, sooner or later.
[them] Later, by the look of it.
[them] My pack animals hate thunder more than I do.
[us] They're not the only ones.
[them] Then we'll all sulk together until it's over.
[them] Snow like this makes the tracking easy, the animals can't hide.
[us] Neither can we.
[them] That's why we walk in each other's footprints.
[them] Hot as a smithy, and me in wool.
[us] Come in out of the sun for a while.
[them] Gladly, before I cook in it.
